title: Managing Public Health and Food Safety Risks with New SAFE Framework
what_it_is: Managing Public Health and Food Safety Risks with New SAFE Framework

sections.label: SAFE framework food safety grading
sections.summary: The SAFE framework, part of SFA's science- and risk-based regime, will be implemented in two phases starting 19 January 2026.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) how will transparency and authenticity of the food safety grading under the new Safety Assurance for Food Establishment (SAFE) framework be assured, given that physical decals will be replaced by digital disclosures from 19 January 2026 onwards; and (b) how will consumers who are less digitally savvy still be able to easily access the food safety grading information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment regarding the new Safety Assurance for Food Establishments (SAFE) framework (a) whether the shift to self-regulation and reduction in regular inspections is being driven by manpower constraints; (b) what is the revised inspection frequency; and (c) whether relying on track records risk making the system reactive, where food safety standards may slip unnoticed until a major lapse occurs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment with the new food grading system announced on 7 January 2026 (a) how will small businesses with limited resources be assisted to meet the additional requirements; and (b) what is the transition duration as well as the resources required by SFA to complete inspections under the new grading system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: It is part of the Singapore Food Agency's (SFA’s) science- and risk-based food safety regime, which aims to keep the number of foodborne illness cases related to foodborne outbreaks low.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: It will be implemented in two phases, with the first phase implemented on 19 January 2026.

sections.label: FSMS, AFHO and Grade C downgrade
sections.summary: Establishments must implement a Food Safety Management System and appoint an Advanced Food Hygiene Officer, and major lapses or 12 demerit points downgrade them to Grade C.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Such establishments will need to implement a Food Safety Management System (FSMS) and appoint an Advanced Food Hygiene Officer (AFHO) to provide better food safety assurance to consumers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Those that commit a major food safety lapse and are convicted in court or suspended after accumulating 12 demerit points from food safety lapses will be downgraded to Grade C, regardless of their existing grade.

sections.label: AFHO training course subsidies
sections.summary: Individuals applying for the AFHO training course will receive SkillsFuture Singapore subsidies of up to 70%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Individuals who apply for the AFHO training course will receive SkillsFuture Singapore subsidies of up to 70%.

sections.label: Risk-based inspection frequency
sections.summary: Under the risk-based regime, inspections are done more frequently for higher-risk or poorly performing outlets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: With the risk-based regime, we are able to now do inspections more frequently for outlets that are found to be of higher risk or who perform poorly.

sections.label: Grade B government procurement criterion
sections.summary: Government procurement requires a minimum of Grade B in the criteria to be procured under Government contracts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Government procurement is one good example in which there is a minimum of Grade B in the criteria to be procured under Government contracts.

sections.label: No self-declaration for audits
sections.summary: For Category 1 and Category 2 classification, no self declaration is required for audits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: To the Member's second question on audits, for Category 1 and Category 2 classification as an example, there is no self declaration required.

sections.label: SFA Point Demerit System
sections.summary: SFA's Point Demerit System triggers suspension, and court convictions also lead to suspension, safeguarding consumer safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: For SFA, we have a Point Demerit System.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: So, the moment that triggers, you will face suspension and therefore, this safeguards public safety, the consumer safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: In the case of court conviction as well, suspensions will kick in as well.
